blocks.title: Triple Tank Trouble – Mechatronic Carnival Game
description: Architected event-driven firmware (C on PIC32) utilizing 3+ state machines for game logic and sensor inputs
Designed and fabricated a 270° reciprocating turntable assembly and a custom pneumatic bellows system, integrating impeller-based airflow sensing to digitize analog pressure release inputs
Engineered the complete mechanical assembly using CAD, integrating the rotating turntable, transmission systems, and lead-screw gear dispenser, adhering to packaging constraints
Programmed custom bit-mapped animations on LED matrices to visualize real-time tank pressure, utilizing non-blocking code to process high-frequency impeller inputs without display flicker

blocks.title: Mars Attacks! – High-Cycle Electromechanical Actuator
blocks.organization: Advanced Mechanical Systems Design | Stanford ME204
description: Designed a 210 grams crank-slide mechanism with rope transmission to actuate a spring load, optimizing for fatigue during a 144-hour endurance test
Validated component integrity by correlating FBDs with FEA to predict stress and prevent cyclic loading failure

Characterized DC motor thermal properties ($R_t, C_t$) to determine optimal operating set points, designing a custom 1200:1 hybrid transmission (planetary and spur gears) to maximize torque within thermal safety limits
Integrated catalog components, applying GD&T and mass-optimization strategies for a lightweight assembly

blocks.title: 3-DoF Robot Arm

Implemented Forward Kinematics and iterative Inverse Kinematics for arm mechanism and made a driver code

blocks.title: Designing of Low-Cost Flowmeter for Subsurface Fluxes
blocks.organization: Guide: Prof. Alain Crave (Observatorie des Sciences de l'Univers de Rennes, France)
description: Engineered a flowmeter for <5% the cost of traditional systems by analyzing a ceramic heater's thermal profile
Designed an experimental setup to simulate in-situ conditions by controlling thermal conductivity, and flow
Simulated 2D heat transfer in porous media using the Conjugate Heat Transfer in COMSOL Multiphysics CFD
Validated a two-part thermal analysis where the initial slope of the temperature rise yields thermal conductivity, while the peak temperature is inversely proportional to flow velocity
